2
What is 0.25 kN mm–2 expressed in N m–2?
A
0.00025 N m–2
B
0.25 N m–2
C
250 000 N m–2
D
250 000 000 N m–2

hints: Notice the starting unit $0.25 \text{ kN mm}^{-2}$ has a prefix on the top with $\text{kN}$ and a prefixed squared length underneath with $\text{mm}^{-2}$.
Recall that $1 \text{ kN} = 1000 \text{ N}$ and that $1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, so $1 \text{ mm}^{2} = 10^{-6} \text{ m}^{2}$.
Combine the two changes by converting $0.25$ to newtons first, then divide by $10^{-6}$ to account for dividing by a very small area.
walkthrough: Identify the given value as $0.25 \text{ kN mm}^{-2}$, which means $0.25 \text{ kN}$ divided by $1 \text{ mm}^{2}$.
State the conversion factors: $1 \text{ kN} = 10^{3} \text{ N}$ and $1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Convert the numerator: $0.25 \text{ kN} = 0.25 \times 10^{3} \text{ N} = 250 \text{ N}$.
Substitute both: $0.25 \text{ kN mm}^{-2} = 250 \text{ N} \times 10^{6} \text{ m}^{-2} = 250\,000\,000 \text{ N m}^{-2}$ with unit $\text{N m}^{-2}$ as required.

A.explanation: This value is far too small because dividing by $1000$ for the $\text{mm}$ conversion is the wrong direction for an area in the denominator.

B.explanation: This ignores both prefixes, assuming $1 \text{ kN} = 1 \text{ N}$ and $1 \text{ mm}^{-2} = 1 \text{ m}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: This correctly converts $0.25 \text{ kN}$ to $250 \text{ N}$ but only multiplies by $1000$ once, forgetting that $\text{mm}^{-2}$ involves a squared length.

D.explanation: Converting $0.25 \text{ kN}$ to $250 \text{ N}$ and $1 \text{ mm}^{-2}$ to $10^{6} \text{ m}^{-2}$ gives $250 \times 10^{6} = 250\,000\,000 \text{ N m}^{-2}$.
